steps.body: Find a number by its row and spot. 47 is in the row of forties, 7 spots across.
steps.narration: Find a number by its row and spot. Forty-seven is in the row of forties, seven spots across.

steps.body: Match each number to its row.

widget.prompt: Which row of ten is each number in?

pairErrors.feedback: 47's tens digit is 4 — it's in the forties (41–50), not the sixties.
23's tens digit is 2 — it's in the twenties (21–30), not the forties.

widget.missFeedback: The tens digit tells the row: 47 → forties, 23 → twenties, 68 → sixties.
widget.successFeedback: The tens digit names the row — nicely found!

predict.prompt: Which digit tells you a number's ROW on the chart — the tens digit or the ones digit?
predict.reveal: Rows ARE tens — the tens digit names the row, and the ones digit just finds the seat inside it.

steps.body: Fill the gap in a row.
explanationVariants: Across a row, 41, 42, 43, then 44, then 45 — the missing number is 44.

widget.prompt: Fill the missing number in this row: 41, 42, 43, __, 45

commonErrors.feedback: 40 comes before 41, not inside this row. The gap after 43 is 44.
46 comes after 45. The gap between 43 and 45 is 44.

steps.body: The spot across is the ones digit. 47 sits under 7. 52 sits under 2.
steps.narration: The spot across is the ones digit. Forty-seven sits under seven. Fifty-two sits under two.

widget.prompt: Drag these into the order they appear across the row.

misorderFeedback.feedback: 47 is the biggest — it goes last across the row. Start with 43.

widget.missFeedback: Across a row, numbers rise by one: 43, 44, 45, 46, 47.

explanationVariants: Across a row you count up one: right after 47 comes 48.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 47 in its row?

commonErrors.feedback: 46 is just BEFORE 47. Right after 47 is 48.
57 is straight DOWN a row (ten more). Right ACROSS from 47 is 48.

explanationVariants: 68 has a 6 in the tens place, so it's in the row 61–70 — the sixties.
The tens digit of 68 is 6, placing it in 61–70.

options.label: the sixties (61–70)
options.feedback: Yes — the tens digit 6 puts 68 in the row 61–70.

options.label: the seventies (71–80)
options.feedback: 68 is less than 70. Its tens digit is 6, so it's in 61–70.

options.label: the eighties (81–90)
options.feedback: 68 is nowhere near 80. The tens digit 6 means 61–70.

hints: Look at the tens digit of 68.

explanationVariants: Across the row 76, 77, then 78, then 79, 80 — the missing number is 78.

commonErrors.feedback: 77 is already shown. The gap after it is 78.
88 is a whole row down. Across from 77 comes 78.

takeaways: The tens digit names the row.
The ones digit is the spot across.
Across a row counts up by one.
steps.teaser: next: the chart's ten-more, ten-less pattern.

concept.body: Slow it down. The tens digit picks the row. 53 has a 5, so it's in the fifties: 51–60.
concept.narration: The tens digit picks the row. Fifty-three has a five, so it's in the fifties: fifty-one to sixty.

explanationVariants: 53's tens digit is 5, so it's in the row 51–60.
The 5 in 53 means the fifties row.

options.label: the fifties (51–60)
options.feedback: Yes — the tens digit 5 puts 53 in 51–60.

options.label: the thirties (31–40)
options.feedback: The 3 in 53 is the ones digit. The tens digit 5 means the fifties.
